page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.114-912 is a large-scale general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by AMD EPYC 7J13 processors clocked at 2.55 GHz, provisioning 114 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading to deliver 228 dedicated virtual CPUs. The host configuration pairs these processing resources with 912 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio across the entire instance footprint.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data storage relies on external network-attached block volumes. GPU acceleration is also absent. The configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external connectivity. Because hardware resources are dedicated rather than shared or burstable, compute performance remains consistent without throttling from resource contention.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the flexible allocation model allows provisioning dense multi-core processing capacity in a single virtualized envelope without paying for unneeded GPU silicon or bundled local disk arrays. The primary operational trade-off is the complete reliance on network-based block storage for disk I/O. VM.Standard.E4.Flex.114-912 is well suited for highly parallelized multi-threaded workloads, enterprise ERP software, distributed data processing, continuous integration build clusters, and general-purpose backend services requiring high core density and balanced memory.
